title: Monsoon and Tropical Cyclone Rainfall Patterns Influence Peak Discharge and Runoff Duration in Data-Scarce Urban Catchments
content: In various regions of the world, the quality and availability of high-resolution and high-quality meteorological data is limited, even though such data is essential for generating early warning programs, forecasts, and mathematical modeling. In Mexico, the official meteorological monitoring network presents issues that hinder the understanding of rainfall patterns and, consequently, the generation of hydrological models. Considering data from a crowdsourcing meteorological network, the temporal behavior of 58 monsoonal and convective storms in the Los Cabos region of Baja California Sur is analyzed. Using 5-minute data, synthetic hyetographs are generated and compared with a centralized model. The results are integrated into an HEC-HMS mathematical model to simulate hydrological behavior in idealized watersheds. The centered synthetic storm produced the highest peaks, whereas monsoon rainfall generated earlier responses and tropical-cyclone patterns produced broader, longer hydrographs. A multi-model framework therefore provides a more realistic basis for flood-hazard assessment in data scarce urban environments.
